title: SSE appendable checkpoints and lazy function-call reintegration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Clients using our SSE streaming endpoint need robust reconnect behavior that preserves both partial text deltas and out-of-band tool/function-call outputs. Current reconnect approaches either force full replay (costly) or rely on heavyweight resume tokens that are hard for lightweight clients to adopt. This results in duplicated tool outputs, inconsistent structured output emission, and poor UX when connections flake.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On reconnect clients can request an appendable checkpoint window and receive a compact sequence of incremental frames that allows them to rehydrate missing text deltas and integrate function/tool-call outputs without replaying the whole session. 2) Function-call outputs are reintroduced deterministically and idempotently: clients must not apply the same tool result twice. 3) Backward-compatible fallback: legacy clients that do not implement the new lightweight shim still receive a valid stream (downgrade to JSONL-compat chunks). 4) Latency and CPU ingress remain within 10% of current for median small sessions; tail latency increase < 20%.
approach_summary: Introduce an 'appendable checkpoint' concept on the server side: periodic lightweight markers that include a compact checkpoint header (checkpoint_id, last_seq, compact metadata) plus a small digest of function-call outcomes emitted since the previous checkpoint. On reconnect clients can request frames starting from last_seq+1 or ask for a 'delta-synthesis' package for missing function outcomes. To minimize on-wire size we encode checkpoint metadata as base64 proto and provide an optional 'delta-summary' frame that describes function-call inserts as stable references (id + minimal schema). Clients implement a lazy reintegration algorithm: integrate text deltas immediately, stash function-call results until confirmation that they haven't been applied, then apply with at-most-once semantics using idempotency tokens.
detailed_work_items: Server: Add checkpoint rotation manager that emits appendable checkpoints every 1-5s depending on session churn
Server: Emit delta-summary frames capturing function-call outputs with stable ids and canonical JSON-LD pointers
Server: Provide a reconnect API parameter 'checkpoint_strategy=appendable' and support 'synthesize=true' to return compact backfill packages
Client-SDK: Add lightweight shim that understands checkpoint headers, lazy reintegration, and idempotency gates
Client-SDK: Provide polyfill path for legacy clients that request 'compat=jsonl' and receive per-event JSONL frames
Testing: Chaos tests that simulate 1000 reconnects/min with random network drops, ensure no duplicated function outputs
Observability: Instrument counters for backfills served, bytes transmitted for backfill, function-insert dedup events
Docs: Design doc + client migration guide + API spec updates
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces full-session replays and makes function-call outputs deterministic across reconnects; supports lightweight clients. Cons: adds server bookkeeping and slightly larger metadata overhead on each checkpoint; requires client SDK updates for best behavior. If clients don't upgrade they fall back to a compatible JSONL stream (graceful but less efficient).
compatibility_notes: We keep an explicit compatibility header: X-RI-SSE-Version and X-RI-SSE-Compat with values 'v2-appendable' and 'jsonl-legacy'. Servers will advertise supported modes in the connection preface; proxies (CloudFront/NGINX) must not coalesce or drop SSE comment lines — we will surface required proxy config snippets in the docs.
perf_targets: Median add-to-first-byte for a checkpointed frame < 8ms on p3-like nodes; backfill package generation 99th percentile < 150ms; average backfill size < 8KB for typical 512-token sessions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint header encode/decode, integration tests with reconnect scenarios, end-to-end harness that replays recorded session traces (real traffic) and verifies idempotent function-call application. Add fuzzing for malformed delta-summary frames. Run comparative performance against current production endpoint on canary fleet.
